headline: Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg said Meta built the Llama 4 team the wrong way and that AI models need small, tight-knit teams.
score_reason: Pool score kept: rare candid admission explaining a major model failure, though the interview date is unclear.
importance_line: It shows why a leading company's AI model fell behind and why it rebuilt its lab, which matters to developers who relied on Llama, but it is Zuckerberg's own account.
summary: OfficeChai reports that Zuckerberg said in an interview that with Llama 4 Meta "fell off the trajectory" it needed, because he modelled the team on large Instagram and ads machine-learning groups instead of "a very tight-knit team". He said Meta then built a new group, Meta Superintelligence Lab, which has since produced the Muse Spark model.
notes: The interview's name and date are not given by OfficeChai. Muse Spark benchmark claims are Meta's. The article also reports an allegation by Yann LeCun, Meta's former chief scientist, about benchmark practices; not repeated here.
